**Finding: Deviation (high severity) — Section 6.1 Exclusivity**

Contrary to the planner's "likely absent" hint, the agreement does contain an exclusivity restraint binding our client. Section 6.1 (paragraph p0037) bars The Deerskin Companies, for the entire term, from participating in any similar internet project involving Deerskin Products *or* "substantially similar" products, and grants HDI the exclusive right to the "Deerskin" branded consumer web site. Because Section 4.1 auto-renews annually, the restraint is effectively open-ended, and the only exit (Section 1.6) is a narrow 70-day launch failure right — i.e., the playbook's walk-away pattern.

I took the fallback rather than deletion because HDI gives reciprocal (and longer) exclusivity in Section 6.3 and Section 6.2 preserves our closeout-site carve-out. The validated redline limits the restraint to Deerskin Products for 12 months from the Effective Date and terminates it automatically if HDI misses the Section 1.6 launch date or its other service/delivery obligations. Exclusivity running in our favour is left intact.
